verdict.rationale: Docusign documents a public eSignature REST API through its Developer Center, publishes OpenAPI/Swagger specs on GitHub that "allow both humans and computers to discover" the service, and ships an official Node.js client and an official MCP server. Independent developers corroborate it hands-on: one built a POC in Postman in an hour and another called the documentation "fantastic in its thoroughness". Some developers report friction (an embedded-flow issue that required a legacy API version, and one calling the API "an afterthought"), but these are specific complaints about one flow, not evidence that the API fails to work. missing for 10: machine-discoverable spec at standard paths (openapi.json and llms.txt both return 404; specs live only on GitHub), consistently positive independent API experience.
